subtitle: One Voice at the Valley Mouth
briefing: Merek’s own force holds the valley mouth. The packs and Old Root now fight together under Ash-Muzzle. Break the chief and his army to end the occupation. Their bows cover the nearest ford; a narrow forest shelf runs behind them, while the southern marsh crossing offers another approach.

intro.text: Yara hides behind beasts while another keeper wears her quarrel. Come across, Ash-Muzzle. I will settle both debts.
Yara does not command me. You brought your spears onto our feeding grounds. Now every den you threatened stands against you.

dialogue.text: The bows cover that ford. Put the old tree in front; arrows bite poorly into its bark. We can follow once the archers turn.

alternative.text: Their bows cover the ford. Let the old tree take the arrows while our thorns work behind it.

dialogue.text: I can hold the mouth of that forest shelf. Send wolves past me before the rider closes it.

alternative.text: A thornshield must hold the forest shelf against that rider. Send wolves through behind the archers.

intro.text: Pack, grove and thorn together. Break Merek’s force. We will not leave a human army on this side of the valley.

victory.text: Merek is dead. His army is broken. Leave the village to its people; we take the southern ford home.

dialogue.text: At the pasture I promised you a hearing. You have my den now, Ash-Muzzle, and my shield.

alternative.speaker: The pack speakers
alternative.text: Sedge pledged his den to this road. We will keep that pledge. We follow Ash-Muzzle.

dialogue.text: And Old Root’s thorns. One call, when the valley needs us.

alternative.speaker: The grove-dwellers
alternative.text: Old Root follows the packs. One call, when the valley needs us.

victory.text: One call, then. But we answer together. Keep the young close while we cross.

debrief.text: Merek’s own camp exposed the claim behind his grief: his brother had meant to clear the grove before Yara killed him. His army is gone. The woodland folk leave by the marsh ford as one company under Ash-Muzzle, with their feeding grounds free of the occupation.

Merek’s army is gone. The woodland folk leave by the marsh ford as one company under Ash-Muzzle. The packs and Old Root keep their own homes, but now answer one call when their feeding grounds are threatened.
